planSummary.scope: Implemented game-wide NOMAD combat/exhaustion plan. Four-second rounds, 100 HP, equipped-only player fatigue, explicit creature endurance, elapsed recovery and durable feedback.
agreedCore: Keep combat rounds at 4 seconds; increase player maximum HP to 100 and rebalance creature damage alongside it.
Player fatigue caps at 50. The tested heavy setup gains 2.5 per active fighting round and fills in 20 uninterrupted rounds.

Every 10 player fatigue subtracts 2 from direct-hit damage after armor/other mitigation, capped at -10 with a minimum landed hit of 1. Bleed and reflected damage remain unchanged in the agreed prototype.

Fatigue per active fighting round is 1 + 0.15 * effective equipped weight, using existing balanced/cumbersome adjustments. Pack weight is excluded. This initial formula is accepted and may be tuned later.
Rest out of combat recovers 5 fatigue and 5 HP per 2-second tick together: 20 seconds to clear full fatigue and 40 seconds to restore 100 HP under ordinary conditions.
Passive out-of-combat, non-resting recovery removes 1 fatigue per 2 seconds: full fatigue clears in 100 seconds. It does not stack with resting recovery; no recovery in combat.
Creatures use their own effort thresholds, whole-number raw-hit penalties and recovery times. The latest 134-profile recommendations are in creatureBalanceStudy.profiles, separate from player rules.
Preserve creature-specific behaviors: heavy knockdowns weaken with exertion, charger openings and existing runner winded behavior remain; no added biological exhaustion for undead/constructs.

Direct-hit exhaustion coverage across opening/follow-up/special attacks and PvP, persistence across reconnects/restarts, and visible fatigue/penalty/recovery feedback are approved. Gatehouse fatigue recovery should follow its HP pattern: automatic ordinary-rest recovery inside, doubled when deliberately resting by the fire.
importantLimits: A heavy player fills fatigue after 20 uninterrupted rounds, not necessarily by the end of a fight interrupted by recovery.
Creature damage is the approved initial rebalance. Automated encounters are diagnostics with two guarded heavy kits, not population win rates or exhaustive multiplayer balance validation.
planSummary.next: Live playtesting and optional tuning; the approved implementation is deployed.
implementationOrder: Settle equipment accumulation rates and verify resulting weapon/armor matchups.
Finish recovery edge rules: gatehouse/passive shelter, weather/fever, death, offline time and interruptions.
Validate damage candidates across more gear, stances, supplies, multiple creatures, parties and PvP.
Implement shared damage/fatigue rules, durable state, 100HP transition and exhaustion/recovery feedback.
Run regression and real multiplayer checks before rollout.

rules.count: Once per actual attack attempt, including misses/blocks; active flight and drake special-action beats also count. Waiting outside the dogpile cap does not count as a normal attack.
rules.penalty: Whole-number raw damage subtraction after ordinary style/crit modifiers and before player armor/stance. Drake special damage is reduced before its own mitigation. Existing heavy damage multiplier is replaced in candidates, not stacked.
rules.recovery: Linear recovery only when no same-room combat target; each profile specifies seconds from fully exhausted to fresh. Player fatigue recovery remains excluded in both arms.
rules.damageTableScope: Exact normal, noncritical, uninjured hit arithmetic; excludes traits, shield blocks, charge/flank and other style multipliers. Encounter runs retain those code paths.
rules.player: 100HP; 2.5 fatigue per active round and -2 direct damage per 10 fatigue for both test kits as a controlled fixed input. No general load formula implied.

findings.recommendation: Use species-specific effort, damage caps and recovery. These first-pass timings are candidates; do not implement the combined rebalance until player recovery and group/pursuit coverage are resolved.

existingMechanics.heavyDecay: Counts landed blows only; raw multiplier floors at 0.6 after four landed blows, fresh after over 30 seconds without landing one. Candidate study replaces this multiplier and adjusts knockdown loss; it does not stack a second reduction.
existingMechanics.chargers: Seven creature templates: existing charge and five-second vulnerable window retained.
existingMechanics.runners: Fourteen runner templates retain existing fleeing/winded rules rather than a duplicate combat fatigue meter.

confirmedPatterns: Short-burst candidate fatigue reached its cap in the tested bear/lion encounters.
Neither drake reached its candidate fatigue cap in these retreating-player cases; peak effort was below the cap and idle recovery matters.
The marsh-hound fatigue penalty never activated in these isolated encounters; short fights ended before its first threshold.
Non-fatiguing creature candidates reproduced existing-rule control traces exactly.

playerPenaltyFinding.withPlayerFatigue: 0 completed kills out of four at the 800-second cutoff; 59-66 fighting rounds and five retreats. Mob fatigue did not resolve this in the tested variants.
playerPenaltyFinding.qualification: Same 100HP and 10-16 drake damage; scripted retreat at half HP, no supplies and no player fatigue recovery. This is evidence that recovery is a critical missing variable, not proof the weapon cannot kill a drake in the finished design.

mobExhaustionStudy.supersededFinding: Forgotten King/Long Crossing deaths in this historical study are invalid balance evidence: the bot repeatedly tried the blocked treasury rather than the open retreat. Use creatureBalanceStudy for corrected results.

playerRecoveryStudy.status: Recovery sensitivity study; no recovery rate is implemented or approved.
playerRecoveryStudy.scope: 100 player HP, provisional mob damage, player fatigue +2.5 per fighting round, -2 per 10 fatigue, cap 50. Candidate creature fatigue/recovery from the roster study stays on. Only player recovery while actively resting outside combat varies. Same half-HP retreat/full-HP return policy, no supplies, two heavy kits and four seeds. Creature flight stops a case; no pursuit or party simulation.

findings.status: Species-specific mob profiles are useful candidates. Combined player/mob exhaustion is not ready to implement unchanged.
findings: At 0.125 fatigue recovered/second (one point per eight resting seconds), poleaxe drake cases reached peak fatigue 47-50, but the direct-damage kit failed to finish the drake in all four 800-second cases.

At 0.5 fatigue recovered/second (one point per two resting seconds), both kits finished all four drake cases. Poleaxe: 23 fighting rounds, peak fatigue 30-47.5. Direct-damage kit: 43-53 fighting rounds, peak fatigue 35-50.
At 0.5/second there were no timeouts across the eight tested creatures and two kits: 62 kills and two creature escapes in 64 cases. These are diagnostic counts, not estimated win rates.
Recovery at 0.25/second remained insufficient for several direct-damage boss cases, including three of four base-drake and all four Woodward cases.

The agreed flat damage penalty affects direct-hit builds much more than builds with bleeding/reflection. Recovery alone did not meet both goals of reliable encounter completion and full exhaustion near the end of every tested poleaxe drake encounter.
Twenty uninterrupted fighting rounds still reaches full player exhaustion at +2.5 per round. Once rest removes fatigue, twenty total rounds split across retreats no longer guarantees full exhaustion.
findings.nextDecision: Choose the intended relation between partial recovery and fatigue penalties across weapon families. Keep 100HP and four-second rounds; do not quietly change the approved -2 steps or guarantee all loadouts have the poleaxe kill time.
findings.mobProfileRecommendation: Keep the per-species candidate table for further tuning; preserve existing undead, charger and fleeing identities. Entry/exit attacks, pursuit, groups and the 13 ambiguous creature identities remain explicit follow-up scope.

restRecovery.status: Approved targets; local test only, not implemented in gameplay.
restRecovery.return: Both HP full and fatigue zero; recovery occurs together while resting out of combat.

approvedRestStudy.status: User-approved recovery targets tested locally; gameplay unchanged.
approvedRestStudy.scope: 100 HP, four-second combat rounds, +2.5 player fatigue per fighting round, -2 direct damage per 10 fatigue. Same provisional mob damage and candidate mob fatigue/recovery. Two heavy kits, four seeds, retreat at half HP; return once HP and fatigue recover. Ordinary active rest only; existing weather/fever effects retained. Gate fire tuning excluded. Isolated revealed encounters, no supplies or pursuit, 800-second cutoff; diagnostic outcomes, not win-rate estimates.
findings: 128 local encounters across 16 creatures, two heavy kits and four seeds: 111 kills, 13 creature escapes, 4 player deaths, no 800-second timeouts. Escapes are not kills; no pursuit was simulated.
Base drake: poleaxe kit killed in 22-27 active rounds, 112-128 seconds including one retreat; Long Crossing kit killed in 43-56 active rounds, 240-288 seconds including three retreats.
Fast recovery still means the poleaxe kit never reached full fatigue against the drake in these four seeds (peak 30-47.5 of 50). It does not guarantee full exhaustion by the end of a boss fight.
All four player deaths were Long Crossing against Forgotten King, matching the prior four no-recovery candidate controls. Rest speed cannot help a case with no successful retreat.
Only ordinary active rest uses the new 5 HP per two seconds. Gate fire/passive shelter tuning remains unresolved; weather and fever can still lengthen ordinary healing.
approvedRestStudy.supersededFinding: Forgotten King/Long Crossing deaths in this historical study are invalid balance evidence: the bot repeatedly tried the blocked treasury rather than the open retreat. Use creatureBalanceStudy for corrected results.

passiveFatigueRecovery.status: Approved; included in the latest creature encounter study, with isolated idle/offline recovery validation still pending. Not implemented in gameplay.
passiveFatigueRecovery.condition: Player is outside combat and is not resting.
passiveFatigueRecovery.stacking: Use either passive recovery or resting recovery, never both; neither applies during combat.
passiveFatigueRecovery.hp: This addition changes exhaustion recovery only.

remainingWork.work: Optional live playtesting across additional stances, supplies, parties and pursuit. The initial implemented values can be tuned without changing four-second rounds.

creatureBalanceStudy.status: These explicit profiles are now the implemented initial endurance values. Historical prototype observations below remain labelled; latest.json.production contains the production verification.

rules.player: 100 HP; 4-second rounds; +2.5 fatigue per round; -2 direct damage per 10 fatigue; active rest recovers 5 fatigue and 5 HP per 2 seconds, passive recovery 1 fatigue per 2 seconds out of combat. Same two heavy kits and guarded stance, four seeds.
rules.mob: Species-specific effort caps, raw-damage losses and recovery times. Count each attack attempt at most once per combat beat; flier and drake active special beats count. Replace existing heavy damage decay; do not stack it. Recovery requires no combat target. Movement/pursuit fatigue still needs separate validation.
rules.damageTable: Normal noncritical uninjured template hits after boss phase, then fatigue, armor and stance. Existing styles, criticals, traits, special damage and wounds remain present in encounter runs; table is not their combined damage.

No party or multi-attacker validation; equipment-to-fatigue formula still fixed at heavy-kit input.
The chainman can spawn anywhere in production; its constructed specimen uses the carrier habitat for this test.
Ordinary rest only, existing weather/fever effects retained; gate-fire tuning excluded.
findings: Creature-specific endurance is recommended: separate effort thresholds, integer raw-hit reductions and recovery times; no player 50-point meter, -10 damage cap or player rest rates are copied to mobs.

688 valid paired encounters cover 43 creatures, two guarded heavy kits and four seeds. Existing mob rules: 272 kills and 72 creature escapes. Candidate mob rules: 273 kills and 71 escapes. Neither arm has a player death or timeout after correcting the retreat policy. These are diagnostic counts, not win rates; escapes are not kills.

Base drake candidate: poleaxe 22-27 fighting rounds, 112-128 seconds, one retreat; Long Crossing 43-56 fighting rounds, 240-288 seconds, three retreats. Its fatigue affected hits in all eight cases but never reached the full 30-effort cap. Pale drake reached its 24-effort cap in all four Long Crossing cases.

Cave lion and Chain-breaker reached full creature fatigue in every candidate run; Baited Bear in seven of eight. Three-hound fatigue affected seven of eight cases without reaching its cap. Marsh-hound and road-carrier encounters ended before the first penalty; this is expected for short fights, not evidence their long-fight thresholds are calibrated.

After 11 armor and guarded stance, normal fresh/tired hits are 2-4 / 1-3 HP for cave lion, 2-5 / 1-3 for Baited Bear, 3-5 / 1-3 for Chain-breaker, and 3-5 / 2-4 for base drake before boss phase escalation. Crits, wounds and special abilities are separate.

All 13 previously deferred identities now have explicit recommendations: rag-and-bone 16 efforts/-2 raw/40-second recovery; road-carrier 32/-2/32 seconds; the remaining 11 retain existing behavior without biological fatigue. These are design recommendations, not new undead tags or approved lore changes.

Forgotten King was not a demonstrated damage-balance failure: the old bot tried entering his blocked treasury instead of retreating north. The corrected bot also resumes rest after a rat interrupts and is killed. Both kits now kill in all four seeds; Long Crossing takes 25-29 fighting rounds, 140-156 seconds, two retreats. Earlier deaths and the interrupted-rest timeout are invalid balance evidence.

Creature damage ranges were held fixed at the earlier provisional 100HP candidates to isolate endurance changes; no final whole-game rebalance is claimed. Pursuit, multiplayer, other gear and stances, and full opening/exit damage coverage remain unvalidated.

equipmentStudy.status: Equipped-weight formula candidate tested locally; pack exclusion approved; gameplay unchanged.
equipmentStudy.scope: Current game source and migrated database; 100 player HP, 4-second combat rounds, approved player recovery and creature fatigue candidates. Nine actual equipped sets, seven creatures, four seeds; compare fixed 2.5/round against equipped-only formula. Fresh gear, guarded stance, no supplies; retreat at half HP and return once HP/fatigue recover. Creature escapes stop the test, no pursuit; 800-second cutoff. No pack contribution to fatigue; existing pack effects on dodge/noise/escape unchanged.
findings: Recommended candidate: 1 + 0.15 * effective equipped weight fatigue per active fighting round. Uses existing wornWeight, including weapon/shield and balanced/cumbersome adjustments. Pack exclusion is user-approved; the numeric formula remains a recommendation.

504 comparisons: nine real equipment sets, seven creatures, four seeds, fixed 2.5 versus equipped formula. Formula: 224 kills, 28 creature escapes; fixed: 218 kills, 34 escapes. No player deaths or timeouts in either arm. Diagnostic counts only; no claim of game-wide win rates.
Weight-10 heavy poleaxe and Long Crossing sets reproduce identical combat timelines under the formula and fixed 2.5 control, across all seven creatures/four seeds (56 matched controls).

Against base drake, light poleaxe (weight 4) changes from 23-27 to 21-23 fighting rounds, medium poleaxe (weight 6) from 25-29 to 23-26; heavy poleaxe stays 22-27. Light Long Crossing (weight 5) changes from 41-48 to 33-43; medium (weight 7) from 47-55 to 39-44; heavy stays 43-56.

A weight-15 axe/wall-shield set gains 3.25 fatigue per round and reaches full fatigue after 16 uninterrupted rounds; all four drake cases still finish. Weight-2 fast-blade gear gains 1.3 and fills after 39 uninterrupted rounds.

Damage penalties remain whole-number steps of -2 per 10 fatigue, after mitigation, with the existing minimum-one floor. Fractional fatigue must accumulate rather than being rounded to whole points every round.
Pack gear still affects existing dodge/noise/escape mechanics; this change excludes it specifically from new exhaustion. Recovery rates remain the approved fixed rates regardless of gear.

Tests use guarded stance, fresh equipment and no consumables. Other stances, worn/rolled combat gear, multiplayer and pursuit still require validation. Current production source changed since the prior creature study, so both controls were rerun against current source.

recoveryRulesReview.status: Accepted recommendations implemented locally. Real tick/lifecycle checks are in check.mjs.

ordinaryRest.condition: Actively resting outside combat. HP and fatigue recover simultaneously.

gateFireRest.reason: Apply the same 2x deliberate-fire-rest bonus as HP recovery. Exact 10-second fatigue duration is derived from the accepted cap and doubled ordinary-rest rate.

gateShelterWithoutRest.reason: Follow the HP gatehouse pattern requested by the user: being safely inside provides the ordinary-rest rate automatically. Exact 20-second fatigue duration is derived from the accepted 50-point cap and 2.5/second ordinary-rest rate.

recommendations.weatherAndFever: Retain current HP-healing modifiers and protective gear/shelter effects. Do not apply them to the new fatigue recovery rates initially. Ordinary 40-second HP recovery describes unmodified conditions.
recommendations.death: Respawn at full HP and zero fatigue, matching existing full-body restoration. Keep all current inventory/death consequences.
recommendations.offline: Once the body actually leaves the simulation, recover fatigue at 0.5 per real second, capped at the remaining fatigue. No offline HP healing and no 20-second resting bonus. Do not count disconnected time as safe/offline while a live body is still fighting.
recommendations.reconnectAndRestart: Reconnect and tab replacement copy the live body fatigue first. A server wake restores persisted fatigue, recovery mode and accounting timestamp; it must not zero fatigue or treat a freshly cleared transient target as proof of safety.
recommendations.restCompletion: HP filling does not end rest while fatigue remains. Allow rest at full HP. Rise automatically once both are recovered, with player interruption always allowed.
recommendations.interruptions: Retain existing movement/effort interruptions; acquiring combat stops recovery even before a hit lands. Recovery resumes at passive speed when out of combat; deliberate rest is a player command, not automatic after an ambush.
recommendations.timing: Use elapsed-time accounting across recovery-mode changes, not one recovery unit per alarm. Preserve fractions and clamp to zero/max HP. Reconcile on commands and schedule completion deadlines as needed so idle alarm cadence does not lengthen the promised recovery duration.

codeFindings.finding: HP healing is gated by hp < maxHp and HP-full currently ends rest. Fatigue needs an independent path, outside weather-skip continue and HP-only guards.
Active rest keeps 2-second ticks hot, but idle cadence is 15 seconds. A fixed subtraction per tick would incorrectly slow passive recovery.
Fire rest currently heals twice as fast as ordinary rest; standing gatehouse shelter heals at the ordinary rate.

Cold skips half of ordinary healing ticks; wind+cold skips 75%, modified by clothing/rain. Wind plus sodden multiplier gives 1.3125, so chance always skips HP healing. Fever multiplies healing by 0.35. These are existing mechanics, not new exhaustion penalties.
buildSession resets resting and combat state. New fatigue and recovery clocks must be persisted and restored explicitly.
Live/displaced-body reconnect explicitly copies selected fields; add fatigue and its accounting state here to prevent stale-row recovery.
onLeave deletes the session before its final player save; do not make fatigue saving depend on finding that session in the map. Save an explicit complete player-state payload.

Existing linkdead expiry clears linkdeadUntil then calls onLeave, which restarts the timer if a creature fight remains live. Reproduced against the extracted actual onLeave method with mocked storage/feed dependencies.
The disconnect fightLive checks omit PvP targets, unlike inCombat. Use a consistent combat predicate when integrating fatigue/offline rules and validate PvP disconnect handling.

Legacy creature fatigue is excluded from dirty-state detection. New creature exhaustion must persist deliberately and recover from timestamps; a restart must not restore stale effort without reconciliation.

persistenceRequirements: Persist player fatigue units, accounted-at time and recovery mode alongside player state; use explicit saves on transitions/death/leave and the existing retry path.
Avoid replaying elapsed time twice during mode changes, reconnect or server wake.
Apply passive offline recovery only after actual fade time; keep fighting bodies on normal combat accounting.
Preserve creature effort/last-accounted time with authoritative creature state, separate from legacy heavy fatigue if that field remains.
verification: Read current rest command, HP tick, worldIsHot, onLeave/linkdead loop, reconnect displacement, hydrateSessions/buildSession, death reset and player save code.
Actual extracted onLeave method: at 100000ms initial disconnect sets 145000ms deadline; running the existing expiry path at 145000ms re-arms it to 190000ms while retaining the body.

Checked candidate passive-recovery arithmetic at 2-second and 15-second accounting intervals: accumulated recovery is 50 points per 100 seconds; completion must be reconciled/scheduled independently of coarse alarms.
